purpose: Tenapanor is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults. It helps you have more regular bowel movements and reduces belly pain and discomfort. A higher-dose version is also used to lower phosphate levels in adults with chronic kidney disease who are on dialysis.
how_it_works: Tenapanor works by blocking a protein in your intestines called NHE3, which normally helps absorb sodium from your gut. When this protein is blocked, less sodium and water get absorbed, which draws more fluid into your intestines and helps soften stool and move things along more easily. For kidney patients, this same action also reduces how much phosphate your body absorbs from the food you eat.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is diarrhea, which can sometimes be severe. You may also notice stomach pain, gas, bloating, or a feeling of urgency to use the bathroom. These effects are usually related to the medication working in your gut.
warnings: Do not give tenapanor to children under 6 years old, as it can cause serious dehydration. Children 6 to 12 years old should also avoid it unless specifically directed by a doctor. If you experience severe diarrhea, stop taking it and contact your doctor right away. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: For IBS-C, the usual dose is 50 mg taken by mouth twice a day, right before breakfast and dinner. For lowering phosphate in dialysis patients, the usual dose is 30 mg taken twice a day with meals. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your situation.
